name: f = x^rho L(x) with L slowly varying
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isRegularlyVarying_iff_exists_isSlowlyVarying {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ} :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ ↔
    ∃ L, ExtremeValueTheory.IsSlowlyVarying L ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, f x = x ^ ρ * L x
scope_note: The equality holds eventually. Measurability is a separate hypothesis throughout the library, not part of the definition.

name: Uniform convergence theorem, monotone case
scope_note: Assumes f monotone or antitone on some [a, infinity). The theorem for measurable f is uct-measurable.

name: Uniform convergence theorem
scope_note: Measurable f on all of R, which is the book's hypothesis up to changing f far out.

name: Potter bounds, monotone case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.potter_bound {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) {a : ℝ}
  (hmono : MonotoneOn f (Set.Ici a) ∨ AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici a)) {δ A : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hA : 1 < A) :
  ∃ x₀,
    0 < x₀ ∧
      (∀ x ≥ x₀, 0 < f x) ∧
        ∀ x ≥ x₀, ∀ y ≥ x₀, f y / f x ≤ A * max ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ))
scope_note: Assumes f eventually monotone or antitone, and gives only the upper bound. The general form is potter-measurable.

name: Potter bounds, two-sided
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.potter_bounds_of_measurable {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) (hm : Measurable f) {δ A : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hA : 1 < A) :
  ∃ x₀,
    0 < x₀ ∧
      (∀ x ≥ x₀, 0 < f x) ∧
        ∀ x ≥ x₀,
          ∀ y ≥ x₀,
            A⁻¹ * min ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ)) ≤ f y / f x ∧
              f y / f x ≤ A * max ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ))
scope_note: Measurable f; adds the matching lower bound and positivity of f on [x0, infinity).

name: Karamata's representation theorem
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isSlowlyVarying_iff_exists_representation {L : ℝ → ℝ} (hm : Measurable L) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSlowlyVarying L ↔
    ∃ a,
      0 < a ∧
        ∃ c ε,
          Measurable c ∧
            Measurable ε ∧
              (∃ c₀, 0 < c₀ ∧ Filter.Tendsto c Filter.atTop (nhds c₀)) ∧
                Filter.Tendsto ε Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
                  (∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ε t / t) MeasureTheory.volume a x) ∧
                    ∀ x ≥ a, L x = c x * Real.exp (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, ε t / t)
scope_note: Measurability of L is a hypothesis on both sides, and interval integrability of eps(t)/t is stated so the integral is not a junk value.

name: Karamata's tail-integral theorem, antitone case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_Ioi_div {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ} (hF : Antitone F)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) / (x * F x)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: Assumes F antitone on all of R, stronger than local boundedness. The measurable version is karamata-tail.

name: Karamata's tail-integral theorem
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_Ioi_div_of_measurable {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
  (hm : Measurable F) (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) / (x * F x)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: Measurable F, no monotonicity. Direct half only; the converse is karamata-converse.

name: Karamata's theorem, converse half, tail integrals
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.of_tendsto_mul_div_integral_Ioi_of_pos {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
  (hpos : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < F x) (hα : 1 < α)
  (h :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => x * F x / ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) Filter.atTop (nhds (α - 1))) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)
scope_note: The tail case with weight sigma = 0. Assumes only eventual positivity. The weighted form is of_tendsto_rpow_mul_div_integral_Ioi, the rho > -1 case of_tendsto_mul_div_integral. The book's statement was recalled, not checked.

name: Karamata's theorem for integrals over [a, x]
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_div_of_measurableNearTop {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {ρ a : ℝ} (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ)
  (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f) (hρ : -1 < ρ)
  (hint : ∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a x) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, f t) / (x * f x)) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (ρ + 1)))
scope_note: Any lower limit a, with integrability on [a, x] (implied by the book local boundedness), and measurability only near infinity. tendsto_integral_interval_div is the same for f Borel measurable on all of R; tendsto_integral_zero_div is deprecated.

name: Breiman's lemma
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measure_mul_div_measure.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X Y : Ω → ℝ}
  (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (hXY : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun X Y P)
  (hY0 : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂P, 0 ≤ Y ω) {α ε : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hε : 0 < ε)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => (P {ω | x < X ω}).toReal) (-α))
  (hmom : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => Y ω ^ (α + ε)) P) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (P {ω | x < X ω * Y ω}).toReal / (P {ω | x < X ω}).toReal) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ^ α ∂P))
scope_note: No sign condition on X, as in the reference. Scalar X and Y only.

name: Karamata converse, weighted tail integrals
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.of_tendsto_rpow_mul_div_integral_Ioi {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ σ : ℝ}
  (hpos : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < f x) (hσ : σ + ρ < -1)
  (h :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => x ^ (σ + 1) * f x / ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, t ^ σ * f t) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (-(σ + ρ + 1)))) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ
scope_note: The range sigma + rho < -1 only; the range > -1 is karamata-converse-weighted. Only eventual positivity is assumed. The book statement was recalled, not checked.

name: Karamata converse, weighted integrals from a
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.of_tendsto_rpow_mul_div_integral {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ σ a : ℝ}
  (hpos : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < f x) (hσ : -1 < σ + ρ)
  (h :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => x ^ (σ + 1) * f x / ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, t ^ σ * f t) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (σ + ρ + 1))) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ
scope_note: The range sigma + rho > -1 only; the range < -1 is karamata-converse-weighted-tail. Only eventual positivity is assumed. The book statement was recalled, not checked.

name: Karamata's tail-integral theorem, measurable near infinity
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_Ioi_div_of_measurableNearTop {F : ℝ → ℝ}
  {α : ℝ} (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop F)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) / (x * F x)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: Measurable only on some [X, infinity), the book hypothesis; no monotonicity or local boundedness. Direct half.

name: Karamata at index -1, integrals from a
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_div_atTop_of_neg_one {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f (-1)) (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f)
  {a : ℝ} (hnn : ∀ x ≥ a, 0 ≤ f x) (hint : ∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a x) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, f t) / (x * f x)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
scope_note: Measurable near infinity, f >= 0 on [a, infinity) and interval integrable from a. Available for every large a. The citation is as given in docs/HIRATA_COMPARISON.md.

name: Integrals of regularly varying functions are regularly varying
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.integral {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f)
  (hρ : -1 < ρ) {a : ℝ} (hint : ∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a x) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, f t) (ρ + 1)
scope_note: rho > -1. The tail form is integral_Ioi_of_measurableNearTop, and index -1 is integral_of_neg_one, integral_Ioi_of_neg_one.

name: Uniform convergence on [a, infinity), rho < 0
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendstoUniformlyOn_Ici_of_measurableNearTop {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {ρ : ℝ} (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ)
  (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f) (hρ : ρ < 0) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
  TendstoUniformlyOn (fun x c => f (c * x) / f x) (fun c => c ^ ρ) Filter.atTop (Set.Ici a)
scope_note: The range rho < 0 only; compacts are uct-measurable, rho > 0 is uct-tail-positive. Measurable near infinity.

name: Uniform convergence on (0, b], rho > 0
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendstoUniformlyOn_Ioc_of_measurableNearTop {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {ρ : ℝ} (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ)
  (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f) (hρ : 0 < ρ)
  (hbd : ∀ (b : ℝ), ∃ B, ∀ y ∈ Set.Ioc 0 b, |f y| ≤ B) (b : ℝ) :
  TendstoUniformlyOn (fun x c => f (c * x) / f x) (fun c => c ^ ρ) Filter.atTop (Set.Ioc 0 b)
scope_note: The range rho > 0 only, with f bounded on every (0, b]; the converse direction of the book, that boundedness is necessary, is not stated.

name: Karamata's representation for index rho
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isRegularlyVarying_iff_exists_representation {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ ↔
    ∃ a,
      0 < a ∧
        ∃ c r,
          Measurable c ∧
            Measurable r ∧
              (∃ c₀, 0 < c₀ ∧ Filter.Tendsto c Filter.atTop (nhds c₀)) ∧
                Filter.Tendsto r Filter.atTop (nhds ρ) ∧
                  (∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => r t / t) MeasureTheory.volume a x) ∧
                    ∀ x ≥ a, f x = c x * Real.exp (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, r t / t)
scope_note: Every rho, measurable near infinity. The forward direction with r bounded on [a, infinity) is IsRegularlyVarying.exists_representation.

name: Composition of regularly varying functions
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.comp {f g : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ η : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f)
  (hg : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying g η)
  (hgtop : Filter.Tendsto g Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => f (g x)) (ρ * η)
scope_note: g -> infinity; f measurable near infinity. The book number was recalled, not checked.

name: A limit of f(cx)/f(x) is a power
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.exists_isRegularlyVarying_of_tendsto {f k : ℝ → ℝ}
  (hpos : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < f x) (hm : ExtremeValueTheory.MeasurableNearTop f)
  (hk : ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → 0 < k c)
  (h : ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → Filter.Tendsto (fun x => f (c * x) / f x) Filter.atTop (nhds (k c))) :
  ∃ ρ, ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ ∧ ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → k c = c ^ ρ
scope_note: Assumes a positive limit for every c > 0; the book needs it only on a set of positive measure.
